text.p: Portuguese bonds followed the lower European trend after Tuesday's fall in U.S. Treasuries and the Bundesbank's inflation warning but dealers said low liquidity was limiting losses.
Ten-year bonds came under pressure but shorter maturities retained some support since the market believes that Portugal's July inflation figure will be positive for bonds.
"Our 10-years are easier but there isn't enough liquidity to drive them much lower and spreads with Bunds and Bonos have narrowed," said one dealer.

"The shorter end of the curve is basically strong. July inflation will be in line with expectations and we don't think the Bank of Portugal will cut rates this month so there is no reason to sell," said another trader.
Analysts polled by Reuters expect the consumer price index to have risen by 1.7 or 1.8 percent year-on-year in July, little changed on the 1.8 percent seen in June.
Dealers said trading would remain quiet until after the release of U.S. producer prices and retail sales at 1230 GMT.
